recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片中央有一團無結構、淡藍紫色的細胞外沉積物，邊界不規則，內部夾著幾個被拉長的紅血球；這種非細胞性的淡藍色物質（箭頭）即冷凝球蛋白沉澱，旁邊白血球與紅血球形態大致正常。
features: Amorphous, pale blue-lavender extracellular deposit with irregular borders (arrow)
Deposit is acellular and homogeneous, trapping a few distorted red cells
No internal structure, nuclei, or granules within the deposit
Surrounding red cells largely normocytic; several neutrophils in the field appear normal
No rouleaux or red cell agglutination evident in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows an amorphous, homogeneous pale blue extracellular deposit with irregular borders that entraps a few distorted red cells, without nuclei or internal structure. Background red cells and neutrophils appear unremarkable, and no rouleaux or agglutination is seen in this field. Such deposits represent precipitated cryoglobulin forming as the sample cools. Findings are suggestive of cryoglobulinemia, which in a patient with lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma is typically a type I or II monoclonal IgM cryoglobulin; repeat smear from a sample kept at 37 C and cryoglobulin testing are recommended.

ddx.vs: Stain precipitate is dark, granular, and overlies cells across the slide, whereas cryoglobulin is pale, homogeneous, and disappears when the sample is warmed.
Cold agglutinins produce clumps of intact red cells rather than an acellular protein deposit.
Rouleaux are stacked red cells with a blue-tinged background, without discrete amorphous extracellular globules.
Fibrin is fibrillary and platelet clumps contain granular platelets, unlike the homogeneous pale blue deposit here.
